submissions.findingTextShort: FDA approved Zepbound for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity in December 2024 based on two randomized placebo-controlled trials.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: On December 20, 2024, FDA approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) to treat moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity in combination with reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. FDA stated that the indication was supported by two randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials involving 469 adults without type 2 diabetes. This is a product- and population-specific regulatory indication, not a generic tirzepatide or consumer-use claim.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in two randomized controlled studies.
submissions.usageContext: FDA-approved Zepbound indication; prescription/regulatory context only.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Regulatory facts can change and require dated authoritative-source revalidation. Draft-only until the repository supports governed authoritative-source receipts.

submissions.findingTextShort: The 2026 FDA Zepbound label retains the boxed thyroid C-cell tumor warning while marking suicidal-behavior/ideation warning language removed in February 2026.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The FDA-approved 2026 Zepbound labeling retains the boxed warning concerning thyroid C-cell tumors and the MTC/MEN2 contraindication while the label revision history marks the suicidal behavior and ideation warning as removed in February 2026. Current regulatory safety language must be represented from the current label rather than copied indefinitely from older approvals or secondary summaries.
submissions.usageContext: Current FDA Zepbound prescribing-information context; not consumer dosing guidance.
submissions.safetyContext: Boxed-warning and contraindication language is label-specific and must remain synchronized to the latest authoritative labeling.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Label content is mutable. This finding requires freshness metadata and periodic/event-triggered revalidation before publication use.

submissions.findingTextShort: FDA requested removal of suicidal-ideation/behavior warning language from Zepbound in January 2026 after finding no increased risk in its comprehensive review.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: On January 13, 2026, FDA requested removal of suicidal ideation and behavior warning language from Zepbound and other affected GLP-1 weight-management labels after a comprehensive review did not identify an increased risk. Any repository text that still presents the older warning as current requires revalidation against the updated FDA position and current label.
submissions.usageContext: FDA Drug Safety Communication and label-freshness context.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This is a regulatory-state update, not proof that all psychiatric outcomes are impossible or irrelevant. It should only govern the accuracy of current warning-language representation.

submissions.findingTextShort: The public Tirzepatide profile makes mutable regulatory and comparative superlative claims while exposing zero canonical source receipts.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current Tirzepatide profile is PUBLISH/manual-editorial with sourceCount zero and an empty claim map, yet it asserts FDA indications, safety facts, pivotal-trial comparisons, and the time-sensitive superlative that tirzepatide has the largest average weight-loss effect of any approved obesity drug to date. Such regulated and comparative claims should fail closed without authoritative receipts, a verification date, and a revalidation/expiry policy.
submissions.usageContext: Repository governance/freshness finding; recommendationAllowed remains false and no consumer recommendation is created.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The superlative is inherently time-dependent and should either be continuously revalidated against an explicit comparison universe or omitted. This record does not independently alter public copy.
